title: Lumen Grid: Autoscale Override Inspector for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact inspector panel (Lumen Grid) that surfaces autoscale overrides, burst credits, thermal pressure, and graceful-degradation knobs for Dedicated GPU pools. The inspector should be usable as a slide-over from any cluster list or route dashboard; it must let operators quickly audit active overrides, edit override windows, and stage staged canary rollouts with rollback buttons. Focus on a dense information hierarchy that supports triage in <90s and prevents accidental global overrides.
design_notes: Single-column slide-over anchored to cluster row; collapsible sections for 'Active Overrides', 'Burst & Credits', 'Thermal & Host Health', 'Canary Windows' and 'Audit & Rollback'.
Expose parameterized 'Burst Budget' with a visual credit meter and expected latency/cost delta estimate (90s, 95th p99).

Micro-interactions: confirmation modal with reason dropdown when enabling global overrides; inline 'preview impact' that runs a simulated request load and shows sample latency curve from historical traces.
Accessibility: high-contrast meter colors, keyboard focus order documented, screen-reader labels for numeric gauges.
Data cadence: realtime update for host health (5s), aggregated metrics (30s), and audit log (1m).
decisions: Use compact radial credit meter rather than full sparkline to save vertical space after design review 2026-03-03.
Preview impact will be a simulated 'what-if' overlay using sampled telemetry instead of live traffic injection to avoid production risk.
Place canary window editor under a guarded 'Staged Rollout' section that requires two approvals for >24h windows.
No global override toggle on the top-level; only scoped overrides (per-route or per-pool) to reduce blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Slide-over opens from cluster list and docks to right; content readable at 1200px width without horizontal scroll.
Operators can view and edit an existing override's duration, max_burst, and min_replicas in-line and save changes with a single confirmation.
Credit meter shows remaining burst credits and an estimated cost delta string (e.g., '+$0.72/hr') when adjusted.
Canary editor allows scheduling a rollout with start/end times, percentage ramps, and automatic rollback policy; creating a canary creates an audit entry.
Prototype links for Figma and an interactive Miro flow are attached and validated in a stakeholder review with Eng and PM.
